Predict requested origins against a saved fitted or evaluated CLM

Source: R/06-ae_workflow.R
predict_allocation.Rd

Numeric output keeps the prediction result and its separate probability, demand and capacity validity. Raster conversion is explicit and permits one vector only; inspect numeric validity before interpreting a map. Supply/theta overrides are deliberately absent. A changed system requires reevaluation.

Usage

predict_allocation(
  source,
  distance,
  origin_ids = rownames(distance),
  demand = NULL,
  outputs = c("rho", "A", "abar"),
  missing_travel = c("unknown", "omit", "legacy_zero"),
  spatial = NULL,
  type = c("numeric", "raster")
)

# S3 method for class 'ae_clm_prediction'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

source

A selected multistart result, NFXP fit or fixed evaluation with a valid CLM prediction snapshot, for a built-in decay kernel or one declared with decay_kernel(); or a result of spax(), which supplies its fit (or its evaluation when every parameter had a value). A result whose search selected no fit is refused. Older objects need regeneration. The snapshot of a declared kernel carries its code and predicting runs it, so use saved results only from sources you trust.

distance

Numeric requested-origin-by-facility travel matrix with complete facility column IDs. Named axes align independently; requested origin IDs may define a new domain outside the fitted load support. Values must use the saved travel unit; no unit conversion is performed.

origin_ids

Complete unique nonblank requested origin IDs, defaulting to matrix row names. Returned rows follow this declared order.

demand

Optional requested numeric demand, independently aligned by names or positional in request order. Zero is known zero; missing or omitted values stay unknown. It multiplies requested flow only and never changes saved system utilization. Use the saved demand unit and reference period; returned metadata is inherited without checking or converting units.

outputs

Exact requested vectors or matrices. Vectors include rho, outside_share, A, abar, unsupported_contact, A_supported and abar_supported; allocation and flow are optional matrices. rho/outside are probabilities; flow has demand count units/period. A and abar have supply-per-demand units.

missing_travel

Default "unknown" makes a normalized row unknown when any alternative's travel is unknown. Explicit "omit" (older name "legacy_zero") leaves unknown pairs out and flags them as imputed; positive infinity remains known absence, while negative travel and invalid finite kernel domains are rejected.

spatial

Optional one-layer raster template plus separately named cell_index mapping for requested IDs, as in preparation. Saved metadata contains plain geometry. Without a mapping, numeric prediction still works.

type

"numeric" retains selected values, all separate validity flags, policies and unit declarations. "raster" explicitly returns one vector map, so inspect the numeric validity result before interpreting the map.

x

For print(), a prediction: the ae_clm_prediction of predict_allocation(). Its print shows the number of origins with each status, what is known of their demand, how unknown travel was treated, and the range of each requested vector over the origins with a value.

digits

Significant digits of the printed values.

...

Unused.

Value

An ae_clm_prediction, or an explicitly requested one-layer raster. Contact to positive-supply/zero-load facilities preserves valid probabilities but makes unqualified A/abar unknown; explicitly named supported-only outputs retain the zero-contribution convention. Zero-denominator rows retain guarded zero mass and a false probability-valid flag.

See also

Other allocation steps: bootstrap_fit(), calc_demand(), calc_travel_time(), check_fit(), clm_allocation(), compare_fits(), decay_kernel(), evaluate_allocation(), fit_allocation(), huff_allocation(), prepare_allocation()

Examples

# West Cornwall: the small areas and practices west of easting 170 km
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)
areas <- areas[!areas$scilly & areas$cent_x < 170000, ]
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
gp <- gp[!gp$scilly & gp$easting < 170000, ]
supply <- stats::setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg, gp$practice)

# Fit on every other small area; predict the others, which lie among them,
# so these practices are their real choice set
fit_areas <- areas[seq(1, nrow(areas), by = 2), ]
held_out <- areas[seq(2, nrow(areas), by = 2), ]

# A fit to the registrations of the fitted areas' residents, with those
# registered elsewhere as the outside column (see fit_allocation())
travel <- cornwall_travel[fit_areas$lsoa, gp$practice]
flows <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% fit_areas$lsoa &
                          cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ]
flow_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow(travel), ncol(travel), dimnames = dimnames(travel))
flow_matrix[cbind(flows$lsoa, flows$practice)] <- flows$patients
flow_matrix <- cbind(flow_matrix,
                     "(outside)" = fit_areas$registered - rowSums(flow_matrix))
model <- clm_allocation(prepare_allocation(
  stats::setNames(fit_areas$registered, fit_areas$lsoa), supply, travel), fit_v0 = TRUE)
fit <- fit_allocation(model, flow_matrix, output = "flow_outside", loss = "poisson")

# The held-out areas: no refit, the fitted values and practice loads are used
pred <- predict_allocation(fit, cornwall_travel[held_out$lsoa, gp$practice],
                           demand = stats::setNames(held_out$registered, held_out$lsoa),
                           outputs = c("rho", "A", "flow"))
pred
#> <allocation prediction> 42 origins x 15 facilities
#>   origins     42 valid
#>   demand      42 positive
#>   travel      an unknown travel time makes the origin unknown
#>   outputs
#>     rho   0.147 to 0.9912 (42 of 42 origins)
#>     A     0.000187 to 0.001756 (42 of 42 origins)
#>     flow  42 origins x 15 facilities
#>   values in $outputs; the status of each origin in $validity

# The modeled share of each area's residents at these practices, the share
# registered there, and the GP FTE per 1,000 residents attributed to the area
held <- cornwall_flows[cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% held_out$lsoa &
                         cornwall_flows$practice %in% gp$practice, ]
registered_here <- tapply(held$patients, factor(held$lsoa, levels = held_out$lsoa), sum)
head(cbind(contact = pred$outputs$rho,
           observed = registered_here / held_out$registered,
           fte_per_1000 = 1000 * pred$outputs$A))
#>             contact  observed fte_per_1000
#> E01018861 0.9667815 0.9945088     1.550514
#> E01018863 0.9747945 0.9979242     1.385976
#> E01018865 0.9904890 0.9911318     1.129310
#> E01018868 0.9889620 0.9973118     1.153529
#> E01018870 0.9897772 0.9938229     1.147452
#> E01018872 0.9870558 0.6741517     1.203248
table(pred$validity$status)
#> 
#> valid 
#>    42
